title: Nvidia partners with Wall Street giants to raise $500 billion for AI buildout
author: D
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Nvidia is joining forces with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital for artificial-intelligence infrastructure. The initiative will create independent “compute financing” platforms designed to fund data centers, chips, networking equipment and power systems.

The arrangement addresses a constraint on the AI boom: even companies convinced of AI’s value may struggle to finance the enormous upfront cost of computing capacity. By connecting Nvidia customers with institutional money, the partners could broaden access to infrastructure for AI laboratories, cloud providers, enterprises and governments. Nvidia says the platforms should offer capital at competitive rates, although commitments and deployment schedules have not been disclosed.

For Nvidia, the strategy extends its influence beyond selling processors. It helps customers purchase Nvidia-based systems while limiting how much financing the chipmaker must carry itself. Chief Executive Jensen Huang said Nvidia could backstop as much as 25% of potential transactions, leaving most capital to outside investors.

Wall Street gains exposure to a fast-growing category of physical assets that can generate revenue through long-term compute contracts. Pension funds, insurers and sovereign-wealth investors may ultimately participate through loans, funds or securitized GPU-backed cash flows.

The opportunity comes with risks. AI hardware depreciates quickly, electricity and construction costs are volatile, and future demand may not justify today’s spending. Critics may also question whether vendor-supported financing artificially sustains chip sales. The plan’s credibility will therefore depend on independent underwriting, transparent structures and durable customer demand—not simply the scale of the headline figure.
